beliefs: The box splits input on whitespace into words, collapsing runs and stripping leading/trailing whitespace [E2, E3]
Empty or all-whitespace input maps to empty string [E1, E2]
The first word is transformed by removing all trailing 'o' characters, then reversing the remainder [E7, E8, E9, E10]
Removing trailing 'o's applies to any word, not just those containing 'o' at the end after other letters: 'xooox'->'x', 'xooxo'->'x', 'xooxx'->'xoo' [E10]
If the first word is entirely 'o's, removing all trailing o's leaves empty, but observed output is 'o' — so at least one 'o' is kept when the word is all o's [E9]
The remaining words are concatenated (no spaces) and reversed as a single chunk [E5, E6]
When there is only one word, output is just the transformed first word [E1, E4]
When there are multiple words, output is transformed-first-word + ' ' + reversed(concatenation of remaining words) [E3, E4, E6]
Case and symbols are preserved within each reversed chunk [E1, E3, E4]
Punctuation attached to a word stays attached and is reversed with the word [E3, E4]
Exact rule for all-'o' words is uncertain: 'o'->'o', 'oo'->'o', 'ooo'->'o' suggests keeping exactly one 'o' when all chars are 'o'? [E9]
notes: Replaced the vague first-word rule with: strip all trailing 'o' chars then reverse, except all-'o' words yield 'o'. This explains hello->oleh, world->dlrow, xooxo->ox, xooox->ox, and the all-o cases.
